analysis.investment_thesis: ACE Alpha Tech fails nearly every Graham quantitative filter — ROE of 0.41% indicates negligible earning power, and the P/E of 12.4 on such trivial earnings implies the stock is expensive relative to true profitability. A tiny ₹156 Cr consultancy with no demonstrable earnings record offers no margin of safety.
key_strengths: P/E of 12.4 is nominally below my 15 threshold
Promoter holding of 43.90% indicates some owner skin-in-the-game
Low institutional ownership (FII 0.19%) means no crowded momentum trade
key_risks: ROE of 0.41% is effectively zero — the business barely earns on capital
Recent listing / micro-cap with no 3-5 year proven earnings history visible
Consultancy business with no moat, no tangible assets, no dividend data provided
red_flags: ROE below risk-free rate — capital is being destroyed in real terms
No earnings track record disclosed; IPO/recent listing speculation risk
No balance sheet data — current ratio, D/E, book value all unknown; cannot verify solvency
Business description (legal/accounting/consultancy) inconsistent with 'IT - Software' classification — categorization ambiguity
analysis.detailed_analysis:
From a Graham perspective this is a speculation, not an investment. The P/E of 12.4 is superficially attractive, but an ROE of 0.41% tells me earnings are a rounding error — on a ₹156 Cr market cap the company earns roughly ₹12.6 Cr at that P/E, but ROE near zero implies either a bloated equity base or razor-thin, unstable profits. I have no visibility into book value, current ratio, debt-to-equity, interest coverage, or dividend history — all of which I require before committing a rupee. The Graham Number cannot even be computed with the data given.

Furthermore, the business itself — a micro-cap consultancy incorporated in 2012 and only recently visible on the exchange — has none of the durability I demand: no tangible asset backing, no multi-decade earnings record, no dividend stream. Mr. Market is offering this at a price with zero margin of safety against operational stumbles. I would avoid entirely and redirect capital toward established enterprises trading near or below book value with proven earning power.
